<!-- Title: [Perf] speculative: Fuse the draft proposal's Gumbel-max sample into one pass -->

## Motivation

With `--speculative-use-rejection-sampling`, every EAGLE/MTP draft step samples its proposal with the exponential-race form of Gumbel-max (`spec_utils.fast_sample`, unseeded path):

```python
q = torch.empty_like(probs, dtype=torch.float32).exponential_(1.0)
q.clamp_min_(torch.finfo(torch.float32).tiny)
scores = probs.float() / q
sample_index = sampling_argmax(scores)
```

Each step reads and writes a `[bs, vocab]` FP32 tensor three times after the draw (`clamp_min_`, the division into a new `scores` buffer, the argmax). A chain with `--speculative-num-steps N` samples N times per verify cycle. With 150K-250K vocabularies and many running requests, that is a visible slice of the cycle.

Upstream already has the one-pass building block: `sglang.kernels.ops.speculative.row_argmax.div_argmax`, a Triton row-wise `(x / divisor).argmax(-1)` with IEEE division, used by the Gemma 4 diffusion sampler for the same exponential race.

## Modifications

- `div_argmax(x, divisor, *, divisor_min=None, ignore_nan=False)` gains two keyword options. The defaults keep today's behaviour:
  - `divisor_min` applies `divisor.clamp_min(divisor_min)` inside the kernel, with `clamp_min`'s rule (a NaN divisor stays NaN);
  - `ignore_nan` makes a NaN quotient never win. That is the rule of the CUDA `sampling.argmax` kernel `fast_sample` uses today (strict `>` scan from -inf, lowest index on ties, index 0 for a row with nothing above -inf). By default NaN wins, as in `torch.argmax`.
- `fast_sample`, unseeded path, `num_samples == 1` (every caller in the tree), on CUDA with a contiguous FP32 `probs` of at least 2^23 elements (bs × vocab): after the unchanged `exponential_` draw, it calls `div_argmax(probs, q, divisor_min=tiny, ignore_nan=True)`. The path is taken only where `sampling_argmax(scores)` would run its CUDA kernel (`can_argmax`); elsewhere, and for `num_samples > 1`, the torch ops are unchanged. The sampled index, `q(X)` and the RNG stream are identical to the old path for every input.
- Tests:
  - `test/registered/kernels/ops/speculative/test_draft_sampling.py`:
    - `div_argmax` with the new options vs `sampling_argmax` / `torch.argmax` of `p / q.clamp_min(tiny)`, on random rows, rows with planted 0 / -0 / NaN / ±inf / subnormal / `tiny` / 3e38, and edge rows: all NaN, all -inf, ±0 ties, duplicate maxima;
    - default `div_argmax` unchanged;
    - `fast_sample` vs the old code under the same seed, including an unaligned vocabulary that takes the torch path;
    - `sample_draft_proposal` under CUDA graph capture/replay vs the old code.
  - `test/registered/kernels/benchmark/speculative/bench_draft_sampling.py`: fused vs torch, `marker.do_bench`.

## Accuracy Tests

No output change: for every input, the fused path returns the same index as the three ops it replaces, and the RNG draw is untouched.

**Op level** (`test_draft_sampling.py`, 4 tests; pass on RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell and GB300):
- `div_argmax(p, q, divisor_min=tiny, ignore_nan=True)` returns the same index as `sampling_argmax(p / q.clamp_min(tiny))`, and the default-NaN variant matches `torch.argmax`, on:
  - random rows;
  - rows with planted 0 / -0 / NaN / ±inf / subnormal / `tiny` / 3e38;
  - edge rows: all NaN, all -inf, ±0 ties, duplicate maxima.
- `fast_sample` matches the old code under the same seed, at sizes that take the fused path (64 × 151,936, 65 × 248,320) and at sizes that do not (small tensor, unaligned vocabulary).
- `sample_draft_proposal` captured in a CUDA graph at 64 rows matches the old code captured the same way.

Unchanged and passing: `test_deterministic_fast_sample.py`, `test_speculative_sampling.py`, and the tests of the other `div_argmax` user (`test_gemma4_renoise.py`, `test_gemma4_sampling_cuda.py`).

**End to end vs main (`8d4e1ce4c7`).** Same GPU, both builds in one container, rejection sampling on, server `--random-seed 1234`. 8 prompts are sent one at a time at `temperature=0.7, max_new_tokens=160`, plus the same 8 greedy, and `output_ids` are compared. Servers launch main, PR, PR, main, so main-vs-main and PR-vs-PR show the comparison is sensitive.

| Model | Launch | GPU | Sampled / greedy tokens | main vs PR | main vs main | PR vs PR |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Qwen/Qwen3.5-9B (MTP) | `--speculative-algorithm NEXTN --speculative-num-steps 3 --speculative-eagle-topk 1 --speculative-num-draft-tokens 4 --speculative-use-rejection-sampling` | RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell 300 W | 1,076 / 1,163 | identical | identical | identical |
| Qwen/Qwen3.5-0.8B (MTP) | same with `--speculative-num-steps 6 --speculative-num-draft-tokens 7 --cuda-graph-max-bs-decode 256 --max-running-requests 256` | RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell 300 W | 1,114 / 851 | identical | identical | identical |
| nvidia/Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-NVFP4 | `--tp-size 4`, NEXTN 3 steps, rejection sampling, the flags of `test_qwen4_exp_models.py` | 4× GB300 | 902 / 979 | identical | identical | — |

These one-at-a-time requests reach `fast_sample` with one row, so they take its unchanged branch. They show that nothing else moved. The fused branch needs ≥ 2^23 elements (≥ 34 rows at this vocabulary), and concurrent sampled requests are not token-reproducible on main itself: 64 prompts in one request, or one request with `n=64`, differ between two main runs. That branch is therefore covered by the bitwise tests above, not by an e2e token gate.

`--enable-deterministic-inference` is deliberately not used here. In that mode every request carries a `sampling_seed`, so `fast_sample` takes its seeded hash path and never reaches this code.

Accuracy evals (GSM8K etc.) were not run: the sampled index is unchanged by construction.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

**Per op:** `python3 test/registered/kernels/benchmark/speculative/bench_draft_sampling.py` (`marker.do_bench`, CUDA graph, cold L2). One draft sample = `exponential_` + score + argmax; µs, main (three ops) → one-pass `div_argmax`. The bench times the raw op at every size; **bold** cells are the sizes `fast_sample` sends to it (≥ 2^23 elements).

| vocab | bs | RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell 300 W | GB300 |
|---|---|---|---|
| 129,280 | 64 | 55.2 → 38.6 (1.43×) | 35.2 → 34.5 (1.02×) |
| 129,280 | 256 | **469.5 → 216.7 (2.17×)** | **159.6 → 109.8 (1.45×)** |
| 151,936 | 1 | 7.8 → 9.9 (0.79×) | 9.0 → 11.4 (0.78×) |
| 151,936 | 16 | 20.0 → 19.1 (1.05×) | 15.4 → 17.7 (0.87×) |
| 151,936 | 64 | **67.8 → 44.9 (1.51×)** | **41.2 → 40.0 (1.03×)** |
| 151,936 | 256 | **623.2 → 269.8 (2.31×)** | **190.9 → 129.4 (1.48×)** |
| 248,320 | 1 | 8.8 → 9.1 (0.97×) | 10.0 → 10.6 (0.95×) |
| 248,320 | 16 | 27.7 → 22.2 (1.25×) | 21.3 → 21.7 (0.98×) |
| 248,320 | 64 | **138.2 → 70.2 (1.97×)** | **66.8 → 57.4 (1.16×)** |
| 248,320 | 128 | **421.7 → 205.5 (2.05×)** | **152.7 → 104.3 (1.46×)** |
| 248,320 | 256 | **1105.8 → 476.2 (2.32×)** | **311.4 → 194.8 (1.60×)** |

On small tensors the split-vocab launch does not beat the three ops on every GPU (down to 0.78×), so `fast_sample` sends a step to `div_argmax` only from 2^23 elements (bs × vocab): ≥ 34 rows at a 248K vocabulary, ≥ 256 rows at 32K. In that range it is 1.51-2.32× on RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell and 1.03-1.60× on GB300. A chain with `--speculative-num-steps N` samples N times per verify cycle (N − 1 draft steps plus the post-verify draft extend).

**Serving:** `python3 -m sglang.benchmark.serving --backend sglang --dataset-name random-ids --random-input-len 128 --random-output-len 1024 --random-range-ratio 1.0 --temperature 0.7 --seed 1 --num-prompts 512 --max-concurrency 256`, rejection sampling on, same GPU.
- Main and PR alternate per rep (main first, then PR first); each launch is followed by a discarded warmup run.
- Change = PR / main − 1 per rep, mean and 95% t-interval.
- Median ITL is the time between streamed chunks, about one verify cycle.

| Model, setup | GPU | Reps | Output tok/s, median main → PR | Output tok/s change | Median ITL change |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Qwen3.5-0.8B, MTP 6, 256 running | RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell 300 W | 3 | 14,728 → 15,468 | +4.6% [−1.3, +10.4] | **−4.2% [−4.5, −3.9]** |

Accept length is unchanged within run-to-run spread (main 5.53-5.69, PR 5.57-5.61). Throughput varies more than ITL because concurrent batching changes the sampled tokens, and hence the accept length, from run to run. The saving is a fixed number of µs per draft step, so it shows end to end only when draft sampling is a visible share of the cycle: a large vocabulary, many running requests, a small or fast target.

## Checklist

- [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit).
- [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests).
- [ ] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations). Not applicable: no new flag, env var or user-visible behavior.
- [x] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed).
- [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance).

Prepared with the help of Claude Code; every result above was measured as described.

## Review and Merge Process

1. Ping Merge Oncalls to start the process. See the [PR Merge Process](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/main/.github/MAINTAINER.md#pull-request-merge-process).
2. Get approvals from [CODEOWNERS](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/main/.github/CODEOWNERS) and other reviewers.
3. Trigger CI tests with [comments](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#how-to-trigger-ci-tests) or contact authorized users to do so.
   - Common commands include `/tag-and-rerun-ci`, `/tag-run-ci-label`, `/rerun-failed-ci`
4. After green CI and required approvals, ask Merge Oncalls or people with Write permission to merge the PR.

+    IGNORE_NAN: tl.constexpr = False,
 ):

+"""The one-pass Gumbel-max draft sample picks the same token as the three-op path."""
+
+import unittest
+
+import torch
+
+from sglang.kernels.ops.sampling import argmax as sampling_argmax
+from sglang.kernels.ops.sampling import softmax as sampling_softmax
+from sglang.kernels.ops.sampling.argmax_jit import can_argmax
+from sglang.kernels.ops.speculative.row_argmax import div_argmax
+from sglang.srt.speculative.spec_utils import fast_sample, sample_draft_proposal
+from sglang.test.ci.ci_register import register_cuda_ci
+from sglang.test.test_utils import CustomTestCase
+
+register_cuda_ci(est_time=30, stage="base-b-kernel-unit", runner_config="1-gpu-small")
+
+_TINY = torch.finfo(torch.float32).tiny
+_SPECIALS = [
+    0.0,
+    -0.0,
+    float("nan"),
+    float("inf"),
+    -float("inf"),
+    1e-45,
+    1e-40,
+    _TINY,
+    3e38,
+]
+
+
+def _bits(t: torch.Tensor) -> torch.Tensor:
+    return t.contiguous().view(torch.int32)
+
+
+def _reference_fast_sample(probs: torch.Tensor):
+    """fast_sample's unseeded path before this change: clamp_min_, division, argmax."""
+    q = torch.empty_like(probs, dtype=torch.float32).exponential_(1.0)
+    q.clamp_min_(_TINY)
+    index = sampling_argmax(probs.float() / q).unsqueeze(-1)
+    return probs.gather(1, index), index
+
+
+def _plant(x: torch.Tensor, frac: float, gen: torch.Generator) -> torch.Tensor:
+    specials = torch.tensor(_SPECIALS, device=x.device)
+    hit = torch.rand(x.shape, generator=gen, device=x.device) < frac
+    pick = torch.randint(0, len(_SPECIALS), x.shape, generator=gen, device=x.device)
+    return torch.where(hit, specials[pick], x)
+
+
+def _edge_rows(vocab: int):
+    p = torch.full((5, vocab), 0.5, device="cuda")
+    q = torch.ones((5, vocab), device="cuda")
+    p[0] = float("nan")  # no number at all
+    p[1] = -float("inf")  # nothing above -inf
+    p[2] = 0.0  # +0 / -0 tie
+    p[2, 3] = -0.0
+    p[3, vocab - 1] = 2.0  # duplicate maxima: the lowest index wins
+    p[3, vocab // 2] = 2.0
+    q[4, 7] = 0.0  # clamp_min makes this q tiny
+    q[4, 9] = float("nan")
+    return p, q
+
+
+class TestGumbelArgmax(CustomTestCase):
+    def _check(self, p, q):
+        scores = p / q.clamp_min(_TINY)
+        self.assertTrue(can_argmax(scores))
+        # ignore_nan follows the CUDA sampling.argmax kernel; the default follows torch.argmax.
+        fused = div_argmax(p, q, divisor_min=_TINY, ignore_nan=True)
+        self.assertTrue(torch.equal(fused, sampling_argmax(scores)))
+        fused_torch_rule = div_argmax(p, q, divisor_min=_TINY)
+        self.assertTrue(torch.equal(fused_torch_rule, torch.argmax(scores, dim=-1)))
+
+    def test_div_argmax_options_match_reference(self):
+        gen = torch.Generator(device="cuda").manual_seed(0)
+        shapes = [(1, 4096), (7, 151936), (64, 151936), (5, 248320), (300, 32000)]
+        for rows, vocab in shapes:
+            logits = torch.randn((rows, vocab), generator=gen, device="cuda") * 4
+            p = torch.softmax(logits, dim=-1)
+            q = torch.empty_like(p).exponential_(1.0, generator=gen)
+            self._check(p, q)
+            self._check(_plant(p, 0.01, gen), _plant(q, 0.01, gen))
+        for vocab in (4096, 248320):
+            self._check(*_edge_rows(vocab))
+
+    def test_div_argmax_default_unchanged(self):
+        gen = torch.Generator(device="cuda").manual_seed(3)
+        x = torch.randn((9, 151936), generator=gen, device="cuda")
+        x = _plant(x, 0.001, gen)
+        d = torch.rand((9, 151936), generator=gen, device="cuda") + 0.5
+        self.assertTrue(torch.equal(div_argmax(x, d), torch.argmax(x / d, dim=-1)))
+
+    def test_fast_sample_matches_reference(self):
+        gen = torch.Generator(device="cuda").manual_seed(1)
+        # Below 2**23 elements and for 4097 (not a whole number of vectors) both
+        # sides take the torch path.
+        for rows, vocab in [(1, 32000), (64, 151936), (65, 248320), (70, 4097)]:
+            logits = torch.randn((rows, vocab), generator=gen, device="cuda") * 3
+            probs = torch.softmax(logits, dim=-1)
+            torch.cuda.manual_seed(1000 + rows)
+            ref_p, ref_index = _reference_fast_sample(probs)
+            torch.cuda.manual_seed(1000 + rows)
+            p, index = fast_sample(probs)
+            self.assertTrue(torch.equal(index, ref_index))
+            self.assertTrue(torch.equal(_bits(p), _bits(ref_p)))
+
+    def test_draft_proposal_cuda_graph_replay(self):
+        rows, vocab = 64, 151936
+        logits = torch.zeros((rows, vocab), device="cuda")
+        temperatures = torch.ones((rows, 1), device="cuda")
+        top_ks = torch.full((rows,), 20, dtype=torch.int32, device="cuda")
+
+        def proposal():
+            return sample_draft_proposal(logits, temperatures, top_ks)
+
+        def reference_proposal():
+            # No greedy rows (top_k = 20), so the proposal is the plain sample.
+            probs = sampling_softmax(logits, temperatures=temperatures)
+            return (probs, *_reference_fast_sample(probs))
+
+        graphs = []
+        for fn in (proposal, reference_proposal):
+            fn()
+            torch.cuda.synchronize()
+            graph = torch.cuda.CUDAGraph()
+            with torch.cuda.graph(graph):
+                out = fn()
+            graphs.append((graph, out))
+
+        gen = torch.Generator(device="cuda").manual_seed(2)
+        for rep in range(3):
+            logits.copy_(torch.randn((rows, vocab), generator=gen, device="cuda") * 4)
+            temps = torch.rand((rows, 1), generator=gen, device="cuda") * 1.5 + 0.1
+            temperatures.copy_(temps)
+            results = []
+            for graph, out in graphs:
+                torch.cuda.manual_seed(77 + rep)
+                graph.replay()
+                results.append([t.clone() for t in out])
+            (probs, p, index), (ref_probs, ref_p, ref_index) = results
+            self.assertTrue(torch.equal(_bits(probs), _bits(ref_probs)))
+            self.assertTrue(torch.equal(_bits(p), _bits(ref_p)))
+            self.assertTrue(torch.equal(index, ref_index))
+
+
+if __name__ == "__main__":
+    unittest.main()
